change: Register-blocked FP32 Conv3D: per-thread accumulation of 2 positions x 8 channels, [reduction][position] workgroup staging with row-strided positions, and a channel tile matched to each layer's channel count.

environment.host: Apple M1 Max, 10 CPU cores, 32 GPU cores, macOS 26.x
environment.gpu: apple metal-3, not a fallback adapter

versusPreviousKernel.input: Public py_synthsr FLAIR.nii.gz, full volume, flip and sharpen enabled
versusPreviousKernel.note: Bit-identical: the reduction order over k is unchanged, so only the execution schedule differs.

versusNativeCpu.note: Unchanged from the previous kernel's 420, and inside the existing thresholds (max 1, fraction below 0.001).

numerics.kernelUnitCases: e2e/gpu-kernel.spec.js passes under Dawn against an independent scalar convolution: boundaries, channel and reduction tails, non-cubic dims, single-channel input layer, fused ELU.
numerics.hardwareSuite: e2e/smoke.spec.js 5/5 passed on hardware WebGPU with real weights: full-volume webgpu and wasm regression against the native reference, TensorFlow fixture parity for both backends, and load/cancel.

isolatedConvolutions.method: One convolution per measurement, GPU timestamp queries, minimum of three runs.

peakFmaCeiling.note: Memory-free FP32 FMA loop through WGSL on this GPU, for scale. The 10.4 TFLOP/s figure from core counts is not reachable through this stack. Two loop forms were measured: 'coupled' chains each accumulator to its neighbour and is partly latency-limited; 'independent' keeps every chain self-contained and is the sounder ceiling. It was still rising at 24 accumulators, so 4.4 is a lower bound. Whether this wall is WGSL or shader-compiler codegen rather than the hardware's real rate is unresolved; separating them needs an equivalent Metal Shading Language measurement, which was not run.
peakFmaCeiling.kernelFractionOfCeiling: The re-blocked kernel's 0.98-1.11 TFLOP/s is about 23% of this ceiling; the previous kernel's 0.60-0.88 was about 15%. The collapse at 32 accumulators is register spilling.

isolatedConvolutions.tuning: 146 valid blocking configurations measured on wgpu and about 190 on Dawn. Dawn's ten best configurations span 240.9 to 250.4 ms on the 24->24 shape, so the shipped constants are within 4% of its optimum and no per-implementation tuning is warranted. Both implementations converge near 1.0 TFLOP/s, which reads as this kernel design's ceiling rather than a configuration artifact.

denoWgpuCli.note: Shared pipeline on Deno's WebGPU, warm shader cache, two runs each.

browserApp.note: Playwright full-volume webgpu regression test wall time on a quiet host, two runs each. The expected Dawn gain is the same order as this harness's run-to-run spread, so the end-to-end effect in Chrome is not resolvable here.
browserApp.conclusion: No measurable end-to-end change in the browser; the measurable gains are on wgpu hosts and in isolated convolution.

scope: One host and one GPU. Engineering parity and throughput evidence, not clinical validation or a cross-device performance guarantee. Historical measurements in performance-investigation.md were taken on a different date and build and are not directly comparable to the wall times here.
